Worst-case estimates. V = vertices, E = edges, n = input size, deg = degree of the current vertex.


## dp_basics.txt

```text
// Dynamic Programming examples

FUNCTION FIBONACCI_DP(n)
    // Bottom-up 1-D DP  →  O(n)
    dp = array of size n+1
    dp[0] = 0
    dp[1] = 1
    FOR i = 2 TO n
        dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2]
    ENDFOR
    RETURN dp[n]
ENDFUNCTION

FUNCTION LCS(X, Y, m, n)
    // Longest Common Subsequence — O(m*n) time, O(m*n) space
    FOR i = 0 TO m
        FOR j = 0 TO n
            IF i == 0 OR j == 0 THEN
                dp[i][j] = 0
            ELSEIF X[i] == Y[j] THEN
                dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] + 1
            ELSE
                dp[i][j] = MAX(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1])
            ENDIF
        ENDFOR
    ENDFOR
    RETURN dp[m][n]
ENDFUNCTION

FUNCTION KNAPSACK_01(weights, values, n, W)
    // 0/1 Knapsack  —  O(n * W)
    FOR i = 0 TO n
        FOR w = 0 TO W
            IF i == 0 OR w == 0 THEN
                dp[i][w] = 0
            ELSEIF weights[i] <= w THEN
                dp[i][w] = MAX(values[i] + dp[i-1][w - weights[i]], dp[i-1][w])
            ELSE
                dp[i][w] = dp[i-1][w]
            ENDIF
        ENDFOR
    ENDFOR
    RETURN dp[n][W]
ENDFUNCTION
```

| Function | Time complexity |
|---|---|
| `FIBONACCI_DP` | `O(n)` |
| `LCS` | `O(n * m)` |
| `KNAPSACK_01` | `O(n * W)` |


## goto_loops.txt

```text
// loop written with labels and jumps
FUNCTION COUNT_UP(n)
    i <- 0
    top:
    IF i >= n GOTO done
    process(i)
    i <- i + 1
    GOTO top
    done:
    RETURN i
END FUNCTION

// retry until the value is small enough
FUNCTION SHRINK(n)
    again:
    n <- n / 2
    IF n > 1 THEN GOTO again
    RETURN n
END FUNCTION

// nested: inner loop is a goto loop inside a FOR
FUNCTION NESTED_GOTO(n)
    FOR i <- 1 TO n
        j <- 1
        inner:
        IF j > n GOTO next
        x <- x + 1
        j <- j + 1
        GOTO inner
        next:
    END FOR
END FUNCTION

// jumping forward over an expensive block, and dead code after a jump
FUNCTION SKIP(n)
    IF n < 0 GOTO finish
    FOR i <- 1 TO n
        FOR j <- 1 TO n
            x <- x + 1
        END FOR
    END FOR
    finish:
    RETURN 0
END FUNCTION

// halving with a doubling exit label
FUNCTION DOUBLING(n)
    i <- 1
    loop:
    IF i >= n GOTO out
    i <- i * 2
    GOTO loop
    out:
END FUNCTION
```

| Function | Time complexity |
|---|---|
| `COUNT_UP` | `O(n)` |
| `SHRINK` | `O(log n)` |
| `NESTED_GOTO` | `O(n^2)` |
| `SKIP` | `O(n^2)` |
| `DOUBLING` | `O(log n)` |

`COUNT_UP`:
- note: GOTO top (line 8) with an exit test -> treated as WHILE NOT (i >= n).

`SHRINK`:
- note: GOTO again (line 17) jumps back to 'again:' -> treated as DO ... WHILE n > 1.

`NESTED_GOTO`:
- note: GOTO inner (line 29) with an exit test -> treated as WHILE NOT (j > n).

`SKIP`:
- note: GOTO finish (line 36) jumps forward; it can only skip work, so the worst case ignores the jump.

`DOUBLING`:
- note: GOTO loop (line 52) with an exit test -> treated as WHILE NOT (i >= n).

FUNCTION MATRIX_BFS(V, s)
    Q <- empty queue
    ENQUEUE(Q, s)
    visited[s] <- TRUE
    WHILE Q is not empty
        u <- DEQUEUE(Q)
        FOR v <- 1 TO V
            IF M[u][v] = 1 AND NOT visited[v]
                visited[v] <- TRUE
                ENQUEUE(Q, v)
            END IF
        END FOR
    END WHILE
END FUNCTION

## graph_bellman_ford.txt

```text
FUNCTION BELLMAN_FORD(V, E, s)
    FOR EACH v IN V
        dist[v] <- ∞
    END FOR
    dist[s] <- 0
    FOR i <- 1 TO |V| - 1
        FOR EACH (u, v, w) IN E
            IF dist[u] + w < dist[v]
                dist[v] <- dist[u] + w
            END IF
        END FOR
    END FOR
    FOR EACH (u, v, w) IN E
        IF dist[u] + w < dist[v]
            RETURN FALSE
        END IF
    END FOR
    RETURN TRUE
END FUNCTION
```

| Function | Time complexity |
|---|---|
| `BELLMAN_FORD` | `O(V * E)` |


## graph_bfs.txt

```text
// Breadth-first search with a queue of tuples
FUNCTION BFS(G, s)
    FOR EACH v IN G.V DO
        visited[v] <- FALSE
        dist[v] <- ∞
    END FOR
    visited[s] <- TRUE
    dist[s] <- 0
    Q <- empty queue
    ENQUEUE(Q, (s, 0))
    WHILE Q is not empty
        (u, d) <- DEQUEUE(Q)
        FOR EACH w IN adj[u]
            IF NOT visited[w]
                visited[w] <- TRUE
                dist[w] <- d + 1
                ENQUEUE(Q, (w, d + 1))
            END IF
        END FOR
    END WHILE
END FUNCTION
```

| Function | Time complexity |
|---|---|
| `BFS` | `O(V + E)` |


## graph_components.txt

```text
FUNCTION EXPLORE(G, u)
    visited[u] <- TRUE
    FOR EACH v IN adj[u]
        IF NOT visited[v]
            EXPLORE(G, v)
        END IF
    END FOR
END FUNCTION

FUNCTION COUNT_COMPONENTS(G)
    count <- 0
    FOR EACH v IN V
        visited[v] <- FALSE
    END FOR
    FOR EACH v IN V
        IF NOT visited[v]
            EXPLORE(G, v)
            count <- count + 1
        END IF
    END FOR
    RETURN count
END FUNCTION
```

| Function | Time complexity |
|---|---|
| `EXPLORE` | `O(V + E)` |
| `COUNT_COMPONENTS` | `O(V + E)` |

`EXPLORE`:
- recurrence: `Traversal recursion: each vertex is entered at most once (guarded by a visited check)`
- recurrence: `Work of one call: O(deg + 1)   ->   summed over all vertices: O(V + E)`
- note: The neighbour loops of all calls add up to E iterations in total (each edge is looked at once), not V x degree.

FUNCTION DFS_ITER(G, s)
    S <- empty stack
    PUSH(S, s)
    WHILE NOT EMPTY(S)
        u <- POP(S)
        IF NOT visited[u]
            visited[u] <- TRUE
            FOR EACH v IN adj[u]
                PUSH(S, v)
            END FOR
        END IF
    END WHILE
END FUNCTION

## graph_dijkstra.txt

```text
FUNCTION DIJKSTRA(G, s)
    FOR EACH v IN V
        dist[v] <- ∞
    END FOR
    dist[s] <- 0
    PQ <- priority queue containing (0, s)
    WHILE PQ is not empty
        (d, u) <- EXTRACT-MIN(PQ)
        FOR EACH (v, w) IN adj[u]
            IF dist[u] + w < dist[v]
                dist[v] <- dist[u] + w
                INSERT(PQ, (dist[v], v))
            END IF
        END FOR
    END WHILE
END FUNCTION
```

| Function | Time complexity |
|---|---|
| `DIJKSTRA` | `O(V log V + E log V)` |

```text
FUNCTION FLOYD_WARSHALL(V)
    FOR k <- 1 TO V
        FOR i <- 1 TO V
            FOR j <- 1 TO V
                IF d[i][k] + d[k][j] < d[i][j]
                    d[i][j] <- d[i][k] + d[k][j]
                END IF
            END FOR
        END FOR
    END FOR
END FUNCTION
```

## graph_kruskal.txt

```text
FUNCTION KRUSKAL(V, E)
    A <- empty set
    FOR EACH v IN V
        MAKE-SET(v)
    END FOR
    sorted_edges <- SORT(E)
    FOR EACH (u, v, w) IN sorted_edges
        IF FIND-SET(u) != FIND-SET(v)
            A <- A ∪ {(u, v)}
            UNION(u, v)
        END IF
    END FOR
    RETURN A
END FUNCTION
```

| Function | Time complexity |
|---|---|
| `KRUSKAL` | `O(E log E + V)` |


## graph_prim.txt

```text
FUNCTION PRIM(G, r)
    FOR EACH u IN V
        key[u] <- ∞
        parent[u] <- NIL
    END FOR
    key[r] <- 0
    PQ <- BUILD-HEAP(V)
    WHILE PQ is not empty
        u <- EXTRACT-MIN(PQ)
        FOR EACH (v, w) IN adj[u]
            IF v IN PQ AND w < key[v]
                parent[v] <- u
                key[v] <- w
                DECREASE-KEY(PQ, v, w)
            END IF
        END FOR
    END WHILE
END FUNCTION
```

| Function | Time complexity |
|---|---|
| `PRIM` | `O(V log V + E log V)` |


## graph_topological_kahn.txt

```text
FUNCTION TOPO_SORT(V, E)
    FOR EACH v IN V
        indeg[v] <- 0
    END FOR
    FOR EACH (u, v) IN E
        indeg[v] <- indeg[v] + 1
    END FOR
    Q <- empty queue
    FOR EACH v IN V
        IF indeg[v] = 0
            ENQUEUE(Q, v)
        END IF
    END FOR
    order <- empty list
    WHILE Q is not empty
        u <- DEQUEUE(Q)
        APPEND(order, u)
        FOR EACH v IN adj[u]
            indeg[v] <- indeg[v] - 1
            IF indeg[v] = 0
                ENQUEUE(Q, v)
            END IF
        END FOR
    END WHILE
    RETURN order
END FUNCTION
```

| Function | Time complexity |
|---|---|
| `TOPO_SORT` | `O(V + E)` |


## nested_repeat_until.txt

```text
FUNCTION REPEAT_NEST(n)
    i <- 0
    REPEAT
        j <- n
        REPEAT
            j <- j / 2
        UNTIL j <= 1
        i <- i + 1
    UNTIL i >= n
END FUNCTION

FUNCTION REPEAT_WITH_FOR(n)
    k <- n
    REPEAT
        FOR i <- 1 TO k
            x <- x + 1
        END FOR
        k <- k / 2
    UNTIL k <= 1
END FUNCTION

FUNCTION REPEAT_GOTO(n)
    i <- 0
    REPEAT
        retry:
        j <- 0
        WHILE j < n
            j <- j + 1
        END WHILE
        i <- i + 1
        IF i < 3 GOTO retry
    UNTIL i >= n
END FUNCTION

FUNCTION DO_NEST(n)
    i <- 1
    DO
        j <- 1
        DO
            j <- j * 2
        END DO WHILE j < n
        i <- i + 1
    END DO WHILE i <= n
END FUNCTION
```

| Function | Time complexity |
|---|---|
| `REPEAT_NEST` | `O(n log n)` |
| `REPEAT_WITH_FOR` | `O(n)` |
| `REPEAT_GOTO` | `O(n^2)` |
| `DO_NEST` | `O(n log n)` |

`REPEAT_GOTO`:
- note: GOTO retry (line 31) jumps back to 'retry:' -> treated as DO ... WHILE i < 3.
- warning: Could not determine how many times the loop with condition 'i >= n' runs; assumed O(n).


## recursion_mix.txt

```text
FUNCTION MERGE_SORT(A, lo, hi)
    IF lo >= hi THEN RETURN
    mid <- floor((lo + hi) / 2)
    MERGE_SORT(A, lo, mid)
    MERGE_SORT(A, mid + 1, hi)
    FOR i <- lo TO hi
        B[i] <- A[i]
    END FOR
END FUNCTION

FUNCTION FIB(n)
    IF n <= 1 THEN RETURN n
    RETURN FIB(n - 1) + FIB(n - 2)
END FUNCTION

FUNCTION POWER(x, n)
    IF n = 0 THEN RETURN 1
    h <- POWER(x, n / 2)
    RETURN h * h
END FUNCTION

FUNCTION SUBSETS(i, n)
    IF i > n
        RETURN
    END IF
    SUBSETS(i + 1, n)
    SUBSETS(i + 1, n)
END FUNCTION

FUNCTION SELECT(n)
    IF n <= 1 THEN RETURN
    SELECT(n / 2)
    FOR i <- 1 TO n
        x <- x + 1
    END FOR
END FUNCTION
```

| Function | Time complexity |
|---|---|
| `MERGE_SORT` | `O(n log n)` |
| `FIB` | `O(1.618^n)` |
| `POWER` | `O(log n)` |
| `SUBSETS` | `O(2^n)` |
| `SELECT` | `O(n)` |

`MERGE_SORT`:
- recurrence: `T(n) = 2T(n/2) + O(n)`
- note: Master Theorem on T(n) = T(n/2) + T(n/2) + O(n): standard form T(n) = 2*T(n/2) + f(n) with critical exponent log_2(2) = 1.000.
- note: Master Theorem Case 2 (f(n) = Theta(n^(log_b a) * log^0 n)): work is balanced across all levels of the recursion tree, adding one extra log n factor.

`FIB`:
- recurrence: `T(n) = T(n-1) + T(n-2) + O(1)`
- note: 2 recursive calls on n-k: the recursion tree grows by a factor of about 1.618 per level, so T(n) = O(1.618^n).

`POWER`:
- recurrence: `T(n) = T(n/2) + O(1)`
- note: Master Theorem on T(n) = T(n/2) + O(1): standard form T(n) = 1*T(n/2) + f(n) with critical exponent log_2(1) = 0.000.
- note: Master Theorem Case 2 (f(n) = Theta(n^(log_b a) * log^0 n)): work is balanced across all levels of the recursion tree, adding one extra log n factor.

`SUBSETS`:
- recurrence: `T(n) = 2T(n-1) + O(1)`
- note: 2 recursive calls on n-k: the recursion tree grows by a factor of about 2 per level, so T(n) = O(2^n).

`SELECT`:
- recurrence: `T(n) = T(n/2) + O(n)`
- note: Master Theorem on T(n) = T(n/2) + O(n): standard form T(n) = 1*T(n/2) + f(n) with critical exponent log_2(1) = 0.000.
- note: Master Theorem Case 3 (f(n) = Omega(n^c) where c = 1 > log_b(a) = 0.000): top-level non-recursive work dominates, and regularity condition holds.


## sqrt_recurrence.txt

```text
// Square-root recurrences  (substitution n = 2^m)
// T(n) = T(sqrt(n)) + 1   =>  O(log log n)
// T(n) = 2*T(sqrt(n)) + log n  =>  O(log n * log log n)

FUNCTION SQRT_EXAMPLE_1(n)
    IF n <= 2 THEN
        RETURN 1
    ENDIF
    RETURN SQRT_EXAMPLE_1(SQRT(n)) + 1
ENDFUNCTION

FUNCTION SQRT_EXAMPLE_2(n)
    IF n <= 2 THEN
        RETURN 1
    ENDIF
    a = SQRT_EXAMPLE_2(SQRT(n))
    b = SQRT_EXAMPLE_2(SQRT(n))
    RETURN a + b + LOG(n)
ENDFUNCTION
```

| Function | Time complexity |
|---|---|
| `SQRT_EXAMPLE_1` | `O(log(log n))` |
| `SQRT_EXAMPLE_2` | `O(log n)` |

`SQRT_EXAMPLE_1`:
- recurrence: `T(n) = T(sqrt(n)) + O(1)`
- note: Substitution method on T(n) = 1*T(sqrt(n)) + O(1): setting n = 2^m (m = log n) transforms the recurrence into S(m) = 1*S(m/2) + g(m). Solving S(m) and substituting back m = log n yields O(log(log n)).

`SQRT_EXAMPLE_2`:
- recurrence: `T(n) = 2T(sqrt(n)) + O(1)`
- note: Substitution method on T(n) = 2*T(sqrt(n)) + O(1): setting n = 2^m (m = log n) transforms the recurrence into S(m) = 2*S(m/2) + g(m). Solving S(m) and substituting back m = log n yields O(log n).


## stack_monotonic.txt

```text
// Monotonic Stack — Next Greater Element
// Each element is pushed once and popped at most once → O(n) amortized

FUNCTION NEXT_GREATER(A, n)
    stack = EMPTY_STACK
    result = new array of size n filled with -1
    FOR i = 1 TO n
        WHILE NOT IS_EMPTY(stack) AND A[TOP(stack)] < A[i]
            idx = POP(stack)
            result[idx] = A[i]
        ENDWHILE
        PUSH(stack, i)
    ENDFOR
    RETURN result
ENDFUNCTION
```

| Function | Time complexity |
|---|---|
| `NEXT_GREATER` | `O(n)` |

`NEXT_GREATER`:
- note: Amortized stack/queue analysis on 'stack': each item is pushed at most once and popped at most once across the outer loop, giving O(1) amortized time per iteration (O(n) in total).


## tree_bst.txt

```text
// Binary Search Tree operations
// Height h = O(log n) for balanced, O(n) worst case

FUNCTION BST_SEARCH(T, k)
    x = T.root
    WHILE x != NIL AND x.key != k
        IF k < x.key THEN
            x = x.left
        ELSE
            x = x.right
        ENDIF
    ENDWHILE
    RETURN x
ENDFUNCTION

FUNCTION BST_INSERT(T, z)
    y = NIL
    x = T.root
    WHILE x != NIL
        y = x
        IF z.key < x.key THEN
            x = x.left
        ELSE
            x = x.right
        ENDIF
    ENDWHILE
    z.parent = y
    IF y == NIL THEN
        T.root = z
    ELSEIF z.key < y.key THEN
        y.left = z
    ELSE
        y.right = z
    ENDIF
ENDFUNCTION

FUNCTION INORDER_WALK(x)
    IF x != NIL THEN
        INORDER_WALK(x.left)
        PRINT x.key
        INORDER_WALK(x.right)
    ENDIF
ENDFUNCTION
```

| Function | Time complexity |
|---|---|
| `BST_SEARCH` | `O(n)` |
| `BST_INSERT` | `O(n)` |
| `INORDER_WALK` | `O(n)` |

`BST_SEARCH`:
- note: Pointer-chase on tree/list node 'x': runs in O(h) where h is height (worst-case O(n) for a degenerate tree/list, O(log n) if balanced).

`BST_INSERT`:
- note: Pointer-chase on tree/list node 'x': runs in O(h) where h is height (worst-case O(n) for a degenerate tree/list, O(log n) if balanced).

`INORDER_WALK`:
- recurrence: `Traversal recursion: each tree node is entered at most once`
- recurrence: `Work of one call: O(1)   ->   summed over all tree nodes: O(n)`


## tree_traversals.txt

```text
FUNCTION INORDER(node)
    IF node = NIL
        RETURN
    END IF
    INORDER(node.left)
    visit(node)
    INORDER(node.right)
END FUNCTION

FUNCTION HEIGHT(node)
    IF node = NIL
        RETURN 0
    END IF
    RETURN 1 + MAX(HEIGHT(node.left), HEIGHT(node.right))
END FUNCTION

FUNCTION BST_SEARCH(node, key)
    IF node = NIL OR node.key = key
        RETURN node
    END IF
    IF key < node.key
        RETURN BST_SEARCH(node.left, key)
    ELSE
        RETURN BST_SEARCH(node.right, key)
    END IF
END FUNCTION

FUNCTION COUNT_NODES(root)
    IF root = NIL THEN RETURN 0
    total <- 1
    FOR EACH child IN root.children
        total <- total + COUNT_NODES(child)
    END FOR
    RETURN total
END FUNCTION

FUNCTION LIST_SEARCH(head, x)
    p <- head
    WHILE p != NIL AND p.key != x
        p <- p.next
    END WHILE
    RETURN p
END FUNCTION
```

| Function | Time complexity |
|---|---|
| `INORDER` | `O(n)` |
| `HEIGHT` | `O(n)` |
| `BST_SEARCH` | `O(n)` |
| `COUNT_NODES` | `O(n)` |
| `LIST_SEARCH` | `O(n)` |

`INORDER`:
- recurrence: `Traversal recursion: each tree node is entered at most once`
- recurrence: `Work of one call: O(1)   ->   summed over all tree nodes: O(n)`

`HEIGHT`:
- recurrence: `Traversal recursion: each tree node is entered at most once`
- recurrence: `Work of one call: O(1)   ->   summed over all tree nodes: O(n)`

`BST_SEARCH`:
- recurrence: `Traversal recursion: each tree node is entered at most once`
- recurrence: `Work of one call: O(1)   ->   summed over all tree nodes: O(n)`
- note: Only one recursive call runs per invocation, so the real cost is O(h) for a tree of height h; O(n) is the worst case (a degenerate, list-shaped tree).

`COUNT_NODES`:
- recurrence: `Traversal recursion: each tree node is entered at most once`
- recurrence: `Work of one call: O(cdeg + 1)   ->   summed over all tree nodes: O(n)`
- note: The neighbour loops of all calls add up to n - 1 iterations in total (each edge is looked at once), not n x degree.

`LIST_SEARCH`:
- note: Pointer-chase on tree/list node 'p': runs in O(h) where h is height (worst-case O(n) for a degenerate tree/list, O(log n) if balanced).


## two_pointer.txt

```text
// Two-Pointer / Sliding Window examples

// ── Fixed-size sliding window ──────────────────────────────
// O(n) — window slides one step at a time; no inner pointer moves

FUNCTION MAX_SUM_SUBARRAY(A, n, k)
    // Fixed-size window of size k
    window_sum = 0
    FOR i = 1 TO k
        window_sum = window_sum + A[i]
    ENDFOR
    max_sum = window_sum
    FOR i = k + 1 TO n
        window_sum = window_sum + A[i] - A[i - k]
        IF window_sum > max_sum THEN
            max_sum = window_sum
        ENDIF
    ENDFOR
    RETURN max_sum
ENDFUNCTION

// ── Classic two-pointer: left pointer only moves right ──────
// O(n) amortized — left pointer advances at most n times in total

FUNCTION TWO_SUM_SORTED(A, n, target)
    // A is sorted; left and right both move toward each other at most n times
    left = 1
    right = n
    WHILE left < right
        s = A[left] + A[right]
        IF s == target THEN
            RETURN (left, right)
        ELSEIF s < target THEN
            left = left + 1
        ELSE
            right = right - 1
        ENDIF
    ENDWHILE
    RETURN NOT_FOUND
ENDFUNCTION

// ── Remove duplicates: fast/slow pointers ───────────────────
// O(n) — each pointer only moves forward

FUNCTION REMOVE_DUPLICATES(A, n)
    IF n == 0 THEN
        RETURN 0
    ENDIF
    slow = 1
    FOR fast = 2 TO n
        IF A[fast] != A[slow] THEN
            slow = slow + 1
            A[slow] = A[fast]
        ENDIF
    ENDFOR
    RETURN slow
ENDFUNCTION
```

| Function | Time complexity |
|---|---|
| `MAX_SUM_SUBARRAY` | `O(n + k)` |
| `TWO_SUM_SORTED` | `O(n)` |
| `REMOVE_DUPLICATES` | `O(n)` |

`TWO_SUM_SORTED`:
- warning: Could not determine how many times the loop with condition 'left < right' runs; assumed O(n).
